transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-23 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 54m
Attendees:
  - Redwood: Jared Kim (AE), Priya Nair (SE)
  - Orchid Therapeutics: Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Marcus Boyle (Infra Eng), Dr. Asha Rao (Security Lead), Tom Elliot (CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Orchid's expected peak/steady-state throughput, isolation requirements for patient data models, and whether Redwood Dedicated or Private makes more sense. Agreed to run a controlled benchmark and follow with technical deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Current infra (on-prem + GCP), model sizes (Mix of 7B and 33B variants), SLAs
- Isolation: tenant fencing, VPC + KMS for keys, SOC2 audit readiness
- Burst strategy: warm pools, pre-warm, autoscale behavior, cold start tolerances
- Pricing bands and contract terms for 6/12/24 month reserved GPUs

Key questions raised:
- Can Redwood Guaranteed capacity isolate DH and PHI models on same cluster?
- How fast can we get an extra 50 concurrent streams during market events?
- What telemetry do we get for audit logs and per-token billing?

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared Kim: all right everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm Jared from Redwood, AE on this, with me is priya the solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya Nair: hey hi, we'll mostly focus on workload patterns and what isolation means in practice, and then follow up on benchmarks.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks, quick context — we run inference for drug-safety pipelines and customer-facing explanations. Models range 7b for quick inference, 33b for richer context. Latency targets: 150-300ms p50, 500ms p95 on the 7b; for 33b more lenient. Cost sensitivity but cannot compromise PHI separation.
[00:45] Marcus Boyle: infra is hybrid — core services on-prem, burst to GCP. We tried a few hosted endpoints (not Redwood) but had issues with tenancy and encryption at rest.
[01:05] Jared Kim: got it. do you have an internal SLO for uptime and some traffic profile to share?
[01:12] Lena Ortiz: we aim for 99.9% platform-level during trading hours, and we have burst events 2-3x weekdays when model explainability runs kick off. we'll send the histogram.
[01:26] Dr. Asha Rao: security is key — we need KMS/HSM integration, per-tenant audit logs, and evidence for SOC2 + ISO in procurement. can redwood support customer-managed keys?
[01:40] Priya Nair: yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS and on-prem key store; for Dedicated we support VPC peering and KMS integrations, and we can offer contract clauses for stronger data isolation. note: sometimes the docs say 'Redwood Reserve' in edocs — sorry that's internal naming mismatch.
[01:58] Tom Elliot: we also worry about noisy neighbors. our compliance team insists that PHI models never land on shared hardware. can we guarantee physical isolation?
[02:10] Jared Kim: there are two patterns: Dedicated capacity with tenant fencing (logical isolation with reserved GPUs) or Private deployment (customer-managed nodes, fully isolated). For absolute guarantee of no co-tenancy, Private or on-prem dedicated nodes is the right lane. Dedicated Reserved can do strict tenant pinning by node assignment depending on commitment level.
[02:32] Lena Ortiz: what's the delta in cost and lead time between dedicated pinning and full private?
[02:38] Priya Nair: generally Dedicated pinning is faster to provision (weeks), Private can be 6-12 weeks depending on air-gap, HSM provisioning. Cost delta: Private carries platform licensing plus infra; Dedicated is usage+reservation. we'll share a sample TCO.
[02:55] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[03:00] Marcus Boyle: for bursts — question: if we reserve a base pool of N GPUs and get spikes, how does Redwood handle overflow? do we provide pre-warmed pool, or redirect to hosted fallback?
[03:15] Priya Nair: options: warm pool (pre-warmed nodes in the same tenancy), burst pool (shared but capacity prioritized for committed customers), or automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant (different model quantization) — tradeoffs on latency and cost. warm-pool gives fastest start but costs more.
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: what's the typical cold start for a 33B model on pre-warmed vs cold?
[03:38] Priya Nair: pre-warmed can be sub-5s for a 33b with KV cache; cold can be 30-120s depending on serialization and GPU memory. note there was a time in logs where model swap had a hang — transcription note: 'k v cache' sometimes transcribed as 'k v cash'.
[03:55] Dr. Asha Rao: audit logs: we need per-request provenance (who invoked, which prompt set), retention of 1 year, and immutable logs. can Redwood guarantee write-once logs to our S3?
[04:10] Jared Kim: yes, we support streaming audit logs to your storage with object immutability policies; for Dedicated we can set ACLs and retention. we'll provide sample schema.
[04:22] Tom Elliot: on SLA — p50/p95 targets and credits. do you have hard latency SLAs per model size?
[04:28] Priya Nair: we commit to throughput and latency bands for Dedicated (tiered SLAs). exact numbers depend on model/sequence length and batching. typical p95 for 7b on Dedicated is 200-400ms depending on batch size and autoscale config.
[04:46] Marcus Boyle: can we do a real-world benchmark that mirrors our traffic? not synthetic. we want to replay 2 days of production traces.
[04:53] Priya Nair: absolutely — we'll do a replay benchmark on a reserved pool; will need your traces and an SLO matrix. that's part of the SE deep-dive.
[05:02] Lena Ortiz: procurement will ask about contract lengths and whether we can ramp down after 6 months. how flexible are commit bands?
[05:10] Jared Kim: we offer 6/12/24 month reservation bands. ramp-down flexibility exists but depends on discount tier. We'll include a 'burst credit' mechanism where you pay less as you scale up beyond reservation for a limited period.
[05:24] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[05:28] Dr. Asha Rao: encryption at rest — does Redwood let us bring our own keys (BYOK) and rotate keys monthly?
[05:34] Priya Nair: yes for Private and Dedicated with customer KMS. rotation is supported; we'll document KMS lifecycle and rotation automation.
[05:42] Tom Elliot: curious about upgrade and model pinning: how do you handle model rollouts and fallback if a new model has quality regressions?
[05:50] Priya Nair: Redwood's rollout supports canary routing, A/B splits and auto-fallback to previous variant if regression detected. We tie quality checks to eval prompts and have a 'safety net' route to a stable quantized model if performance drops.
[06:06] Lena Ortiz: any compliance packages for healthcare — BAAs, HITRUST?
[06:12] Jared Kim: we offer SOC2 and can discuss BAA terms; HITRUST is case-by-case and often mapped as part of Private engagements. we'll share compliance pack.
[06:20] Marcus Boyle: operational question — our SREs run chaos tests; how resilient is the Dedicated orchestrator to instance preemption and node failure?
[06:28] Priya Nair: Dedicated has automated failover in the control plane; stateful parts like KV caches are checkpointed and rehydrated. for spot interruptions we recommend hybrid pools with some on-demand reserved nodes.
[06:40] Tom Elliot: how is telemetry surfaced? we want per-route latency, token costs, and per-tenant cost attribution tied to our billing systems.
[06:48] Priya Nair: Console provides token-level breakdown, trace hooks and per-model dashboards. We can also stream metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana.
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas around model quantization affecting our coeff outputs? we saw hallucinations when converting our 33b to 4-bit.
[07:08] Priya Nair: quantization is workload-dependent. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profile per prompt set; we typically run evals against your test prompts to measure the deltas before recommending quantization for production.
[07:20] Jared Kim: procurement will want pricing and legal terms. we'll aim to share a term sheet with sample pricing by friday.
[07:28] Marcus Boyle: ok last item: network egress and data residency. we process EU patients; can workloads be pinned to eu-west1?
[07:36] Priya Nair: yes, region pinning is supported. For Dedicated you'll get nodes in region; for Private you can run in your own datacenter.
[07:44] Speaker 3: (noise)
[07:48] Tom Elliot: recap – we need 1) warm pool sizing worksheet, 2) sample TCO for Dedicated vs Private, 3) SE benchmark run with our traces.
[07:58] Jared Kim: perfect. priya will take the SE lead on the bench, i'll take pricing and contracting. we'll share compliance docs and three example contracts.
[08:08] Lena Ortiz: timeline: we'd like a pilot in august if numbers look good.
[08:14] Jared Kim: we'll aim to schedule bench next week and lock a pilot plan. thanks all.

End of transcript.
